title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — September 13, 2026
summary: Threat actors are targeting enterprise perimeter devices and cloud identity systems using passkey phishing lures and custom rootkits, while exploitation of critical Check Point VPN flaws is reported as imminent (BleepingComputer, The Hacker News).

tier2.title: 1. Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Cloud Security / Identity

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Microsoft disclosed two threat campaigns where actors abused legitimate third-party email delivery infrastructure to distribute over a million scam messages. The attackers leveraged passkey-themed social engineering lures to deceive users, gain unauthorized access to Microsoft cloud environments, and exfiltrate corporate data.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Threat actors leverage trusted third-party email delivery services to bypass traditional email gateway filters.; Social engineering lures are increasingly adopting passkey themes to trick users accustomed to modern authentication workflows.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The first campaign involved sending over a million scam emails... using passkey-themed social engineering to breach cloud environments.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 2. Dutch NCSC: Critical Check Point VPN Flaws Exploitation Is Imminent

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management / Edge Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The Dutch National Cyber Security Centrum (NCSC) has issued an urgent alert warning that active exploitation of two critical Check Point VPN vulnerabilities is expected imminently. The flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103, pose significant risk to enterprise remote access infrastructure.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 impact Check Point enterprise VPN gateways.; Security teams are advised to prioritize patching immediately before broad public exploitation begins.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The Dutch Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum (NCSC) is warning of imminent exploitation of two critical flaws in Check Point VPN...

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 3. CISA Adds 5 Actively Exploited Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CISA added five vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following active in-the-wild exploitation reports. The additions impact developer software, remote access tools, and network hardware, including JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Includes CVE-2026-42016, an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Artifactory with an 8.1 CVSS score.; Federal agencies and enterprise security teams face mandatory remediation timelines for these exposed components.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added five security flaws impacting JFrog Artifactory, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik RouterOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog...

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 4. Linux Rootkit Deployed on F5 BIG-IP APM Devices, Cisco FMC Bugs Exploited

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Intelligence / Infrastructure Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Security investigations revealed sophisticated campaigns deploying custom Linux rootkits onto compromised F5 BIG-IP APM gateway appliances for persistent access. Concurrently, attackers continue actively targeting unpatched vulnerabilities in Cisco Firepower Management Center (FMC) installations.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Network perimeter appliances like F5 APM remain top targets for persistent stealth rootkits.; Cisco FMC management interfaces require strict access controls and immediate patch verification.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Linux rootkit deployed on F5 BIG-IP APM devices, Cisco FMC bugs exploited.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security
